name: Dune Climb
note: The big climb up the dune face, with Glen Lake behind you and Lake Michigan beyond the next ridge. All soft sand, so go barefoot.

name: Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive
note: A 7-mile loop drive through the dunes with pull-offs, including the Lake Michigan Overlook high above the water.

name: Empire Bluff Trail
note: A 1.5-mile round trip through beech and maple to a bluff over Lake Michigan and the Manitou Islands.

name: Pyramid Point Trail
note: A wooded climb to a high overlook above Good Harbor Bay, North Manitou on the horizon.

name: Glen Haven Historic Village
note: A restored Lake Michigan company town, with the cannery boathouse and an old general store on the shore.

name: Fishtown
note: Weathered fishing shanties on the Leland River, smoked whitefish, and the docks where the boats still tie up.

name: Van's Beach
note: A clear, easy Lake Michigan beach a short walk from Fishtown, good for a swim or a sunset.

name: Grand Traverse Lighthouse
note: An 1858 light at the tip of the peninsula inside Leelanau State Park, with a rocky shore to wander.

name: Peterson Park
note: A bluff-top county park with a long Lake Michigan view and a steep stair down to a stone beach.

name: Good Harbor Bay Beach
note: A quiet, wide stretch of sand in the national lakeshore, with room to walk and dunes behind.

name: Whaleback Natural Area
note: A short switchback climb up a forested headland to a platform over Lake Michigan.
statusNote: Temporarily closed because public access is unavailable; closure posted May 14, 2026.

name: Clay Cliffs Natural Area
note: An easy mile through woods and meadow to the Manitou overlook above the lake.

name: Mission Point Lighthouse
note: The little light at the tip of Old Mission, almost exactly on the 45th parallel, with trails and a shallow swimming beach.

name: Old Mission State Park
note: Public trails, woods and shoreline at the tip of Old Mission, immediately around Mission Point Lighthouse. Use it when you want a walk rather than only the lighthouse photo.

name: Haserot Beach
note: A small, calm, sandy bay beach tucked among the orchards and vineyards near the tip.

name: Bowers Harbor Park
note: A shaded bayside park with a walking path and a quiet stretch of Bowers Harbor shore.

name: Clinch Park
note: Traverse City's downtown beach on the bay, with a pier, a marina, and a tunnel under the parkway to town.

name: Boardman Lake Loop Trail
note: A flat, paved loop around Boardman Lake, easy walking or biking right in town.

name: Hickory Hills
note: Wooded trails and a disc golf course just west of downtown, a quick way to stretch your legs.

name: The Village at Grand Traverse Commons
note: The restored former state hospital, now shops and cafes in grand brick halls, with grounds to stroll.

name: Alligator Hill Trail
note: A wooded Sleeping Bear trail system above Glen Lake with several loop options. Better for a real walk than a five-minute roadside stop.

name: Bay View Trail
note: A Sleeping Bear trail with open high-country views toward Lake Michigan and the Manitou Islands; a strong wine-day hike when Pyramid Point is too far north.

name: Cottonwood Trail
note: A roughly 1.7-mile loop through the open dunes off Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive. Exposed, sandy, and visually unlike the wooded peninsula trails.

name: Esch Road Beach
note: A broad Lake Michigan beach at the mouth of Otter Creek south of Empire. A useful western-edge reset before or after a Leelanau tasting loop.

name: Good Harbor Bay Trail
note: A low-key wooded loop near Good Harbor Bay. It gives a mixed group an actual walk without committing to the steeper bluff trails.

name: Shauger Hill Trail
note: A quieter roughly 2.4-mile wooded loop near Pierce Stocking. Good when you want Sleeping Bear without the Dune Climb crowd.

name: Sleeping Bear Point Trail
note: Open dunes, Lake Michigan and historic Glen Haven in the same corner of the lakeshore. One of the strongest landscape-first additions to a wine day.

name: Glen Haven Beach
note: Lake Michigan beach beside historic Glen Haven and the cannery. Easy to combine with the village without turning the day into a separate expedition.

name: North Bar Lake Beach
note: A small inland lake separated from Lake Michigan by a low dune, so one stop gives you two very different shorelines.

name: Houdek Dunes Natural Area
note: A Leelanau Conservancy trail system through wooded dunes north of Leland. More local and quieter than the marquee national-lakeshore hikes.

name: Kehl Lake Natural Area
note: A roughly two-mile trail through northern Leelanau woods and wetlands around Kehl Lake. A good nature stop on the run to the peninsula tip.

name: Lighthouse West Natural Area
note: A short northern-peninsula trail through forest toward the Lake Michigan shore, close enough to combine naturally with the Grand Traverse Lighthouse.

name: Krumwiede Forest Reserve at Palmer Woods
note: A major forest trail network in central Leelanau with room for anything from a short leg-stretcher to a much longer hike.

name: Chippewa Run Natural Area
note: A compact natural-area trail near Empire that works when you want woods and quiet without spending half the day hiking.

name: DeYoung Natural Area
note: Historic farm landscape, meadows and an accessible trail close to Traverse City. A useful south-end nature stop before committing to either peninsula.

name: Cedar River Preserve
note: A protected river-and-wetland corridor best experienced from the water. This is the choice when the paddle should be the memorable non-wine part of the day.

name: Leland Village Green
note: A small preserved green in the middle of Leland. It is a better slow-down stop than another parking-lot-to-counter transition.

name: Nedow's Bay Natural Area
note: A protected pocket on Lake Leelanau with water access close to Leland. Useful for a short paddle or quiet shoreline break.

name: Stites Natural Area
note: A compact wooded trail close to the Lake Leelanau wine corridor, making it one of the easiest true nature breaks to insert between tastings.

name: Swanson Preserve
note: A quieter conservancy preserve in central Leelanau with woods and wetland character; useful when the goal is to get away from the tasting-room traffic.

name: Teichner Preserve
note: A wooded conservancy preserve near the center of the peninsula with a modest trail and less destination traffic than the national lakeshore.

name: Pat's Preserve at Lime Lake
note: A protected Lime Lake landscape best used as a quiet water-and-wetland complement to the central peninsula.

name: Hatlem Creek Preserve
note: A small northern Leelanau preserve with a simple walk through woods near Hatlem Creek. Treat it as a quiet local walk, not a marquee trail destination.

name: The Narrows Preserve
note: Protected shoreline at the narrows of Lake Leelanau. There is no conventional hiking trail; this belongs in the planner as a water-first place.

name: Pelizzari Natural Area
note: Nearly three miles of trails through meadow and woods at the base of Old Mission. This is the easy outdoor add-on before driving farther up Center Road.

name: Center Road Scenic Overlook
note: A fast roadside pull-off with a broad view over East Grand Traverse Bay. High payoff for almost no schedule cost.

name: Maple Bay Natural Area
note: A protected East Bay property with trail and shoreline east of Old Mission. It gives the planner a useful option for visitors staying on the east side of Traverse City.

name: East Bay Park
note: A compact East Bay beach close to town. Better for a quick feet-in-the-water stop than a half-day beach commitment.

name: Bryant Park
note: A small West Bay park just north of downtown with beach access and an easy sunset stop on the way back from either peninsula.

name: North Park
note: A small Suttons Bay waterfront park that makes an easy picnic or shoreline break between village and peninsula wineries.

name: Bahle Park
note: Local nature trails on the west side of Suttons Bay. It is not a destination hike, which is exactly why it works as an easy leg-stretcher inside a tasting day.

name: 9 Bean Rows Bakery
note: A farm bakery on Duck Lake Road known for breads and pastries. A strong pre-wine breakfast or between-stop reset that feels rooted in the peninsula.

name: Leelanau Cheese Company
note: Small-batch raclette and fromage blanc made on the peninsula. This is the kind of food stop that can turn wine purchases into an actual picnic.

name: Grocer's Daughter Chocolate
note: Bean-to-bar chocolate and confections in Empire. Small enough to fit almost any western Leelanau loop and distinct enough to remember.

name: Pedaling Beans Coffeehouse
note: A local coffee stop in Lake Leelanau that gives early starters a non-alcoholic anchor before the tasting rooms open.

name: Lakeview Hill Farm & Market
note: A working organic farm market with produce, kitchen goods and bakery items on the southern Leelanau side. Useful for stocking a picnic before heading north.

name: Buchan's Blueberry Hill
note: A longtime Old Mission farm stop known for fruit and farm-made treats. Seasonal availability changes, so treat it as a check-before-you-go bonus.

name: Bardenhagen Berries Farm Stand
note: A multigeneration Leelanau farm and seasonal roadside stop. Availability follows the crop, which makes it a genuine peninsula stop rather than a guaranteed retail appointment.

name: Old Mission General Store
note: A historic-feeling general store near the top of Old Mission with sandwiches, provisions and the kind of cluttered local character a polished tasting room cannot provide.

name: Dougherty Mission House
note: An 1842 mission house and historic landscape with a walking trail. It adds real peninsula history to a route that otherwise risks becoming only tasting counters.

name: Glen Arbor Farmers Market
note: Tuesday morning market behind the township hall. A high-value food-and-farm stop if your wine day happens to line up with it.

name: Leland Farmers Market
note: Thursday morning Leelanau growers and producers near central Leland. Pair it with Fishtown instead of treating them as separate trips.

name: Northport Farmers Market
note: Friday morning market by the marina. It makes the long northbound wine loop feel like a village day rather than a series of isolated stops.

name: Suttons Bay Farmers Market
note: Saturday morning market on the Suttons Bay waterfront. In 2026 the market temporarily shifts to Ice Rink Park for several summer dates, so check the market site before navigating.
seasonNote: The 2026 market temporarily relocates for some summer dates; verify the current location on the market site before navigating.

name: Empire Farmers Market
note: Saturday morning market in Empire, useful before Sleeping Bear or the western wine corridor. The 2026 season runs through August 29.
